title: Royal Brief — Morning-Brew Top Sheet
description: A newsletter-to-slide translation with a hard royal-blue masthead banner, a punchy daily headline, and three sparkle-bulleted story teasers capped by a pill-shaped read-time chip — the only template in this category built to feel indistinguishable from your inbox.
philosophy: This template borrows the visual grammar of high-open-rate email newsletters and ports it faithfully into slide form. It values instant scannability above all else, trusting that the reader is in motion — on a phone, on a commute, between meetings. It refuses moody gradients, ambient illustration, and decorative chrome in favor of hard editorial structure: banner, headline, bullets, done. The royal-blue stripe is not aesthetic choice but brand signal — authority established before a single word is processed.
goodFor: Daily internal company briefings and async standup-adjacent decks
Repurposing email newsletter content directly into presentation format
Three-story teaser slides with tight read-time framing
Audiences steeped in inbox culture who expect Morning Brew–style pacing
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly reviews that need full-bleed data canvas
Formal investor or board decks where newsletter tone reads as casual
Topics requiring more than three teaser items per slide without feeling cluttered
Brands with a strong existing visual identity that clashes with a dominant blue-banner structure
author: harness

examples.promptCore: Feels like the very first frame of a high-open-rate morning email landing in an inbox — the banner stripe announces authority before a single word is processed, and the negative space below it is not emptiness but editorial confidence. Mood is sharp-morning: purposeful, zero-ambient, no texture or illustration allowed to soften the signal. Composition is deliberately top-heavy with axial symmetry in the masthead giving way to airy restraint beneath — the contrast between the dense stripe and the open lower field is the drama. Avoid any gradient wash, photographic layer, or decorative flourish that reads as moodboard rather than masthead.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-width masthead banner bleeds edge-to-edge across the top third of the slide with no side margins — publication title sits centered and large within the stripe, acting as the sole hierarchy anchor. Below the banner, an 8% outer margin frames a sparse open field that holds only a one-line deck descriptor or edition tagline, vertically centered in the remaining space. A pill-shaped chip pinning the date or edition number is docked to the lower-right corner, flush to the margin guide. No decorative header band, no footer rule — the masthead stripe is the only structural chrome.

examples.promptCore: Mood of a well-crafted morning email digest — crisp, purposeful, zero decoration for its own sake. Compositional rhythm is strict top-to-bottom scan: masthead anchors authority, headline lands the day's stakes, three teasers descend with equal visual weight, pill chip closes the column. Feels like a high-open-rate newsletter accidentally projected on screen — inbox-native and immediate, not formal or atmospheric. Avoid moody gradients, illustrative backgrounds, or decorative chrome; hard editorial structure carries all the personality.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-width masthead banner bleeds edge-to-edge at the top, claiming roughly one-sixth of the slide height as a hard brand stripe. A headline zone sits immediately below the banner, spanning columns two through ten of a twelve-column grid, left-aligned with a tight rule separating it from the teaser zone. Three sparkle-bulleted teaser rows stack in the central content area with equal vertical real estate each, contained within an eight-percent outer margin on both sides. A pill-shaped read-time or category chip anchors the bottom-right corner as a visual full-stop beneath the final teaser line.
